urgency_rules.description: Periods absent for 3+ months or very irregular warrant timely medical consultation to protect the uterine lining.
Timely assessment can assist in ovulation tracking and cycle optimization.
Schedule a planned consultation at your convenience to discuss hormone evaluation and symptom management.

tests.name: Hormone Blood Panel
tests.description: Tests for Total & Free Testosterone, DHEA-S, Androstenedione, and LH/FSH ratio to evaluate androgen and pituitary hormone balances.
tests.framing: A doctor may suggest checking specific hormone levels typically drawn in the early follicular phase.

tests.name: Pelvic Ultrasound (Transvaginal or Pelvic)
tests.description: Evaluates ovarian volume and antral follicle distribution (the 'string of pearls' appearance) as well as endometrial thickness.
tests.framing: A healthcare provider may consider an ultrasound to review ovarian morphology.

tests.name: Metabolic & Glucose Assessment
tests.description: Fasting blood glucose, fasting insulin, HbA1c, and an oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) to assess insulin resistance.
tests.framing: Your clinician may recommend testing blood sugar regulation because insulin sensitivity is frequently linked.

tests.name: Lipid Profile & Liver Function
tests.description: Assessing cholesterol fractions (HDL, LDL, triglycerides) and metabolic health indicators.
tests.framing: A routine metabolic screen may be ordered for a complete picture.

tests.name: Thyroid (TSH) & Prolactin Differential Check
tests.description: TSH and Prolactin blood tests to rule out other common reasons for irregular menstrual cycles.
tests.framing: Doctors often order these initial tests to rule out thyroid imbalances or elevated prolactin.

questions_for_doctor: Based on my cycle pattern and physical symptoms, would you recommend testing hormone levels or an ultrasound?
Do my symptoms suggest PCOS, or are there thyroid or other hormonal considerations we should investigate first?
What lifestyle, nutrition, or physical activity adjustments have shown benefits for my specific symptom profile?
If I am planning (or not planning) a pregnancy, how does that influence our approach to cycle regulation?
How frequently should we monitor my metabolic markers like blood sugar and cholesterol?
things_to_note_before_visit: Keep a log of your last 3-6 cycle start dates and duration (or months missed).
Note when you first noticed facial/body hair growth, acne flare-ups, or hair thinning.
List any medications, supplements, or oral contraceptives you are currently taking.
Jot down your family medical history (any history of irregular cycles, type 2 diabetes, or thyroid conditions in mother/sisters).

urgency_rules.description: Unexplained extreme fatigue or temperature sensitivity benefits from a straightforward thyroid function test.
Schedule a routine visit for basic blood work.

tests.name: Thyroid Panel (TSH, Free T4, Free T3)
tests.description: Standard venipuncture test measuring pituitary thyroid stimulation and circulating thyroid hormones.
tests.framing: A physician may suggest a simple blood test to check how well your thyroid is working.

tests.name: Thyroid Antibodies (Anti-TPO, Anti-Tg)
tests.description: Tests to identify autoimmune causes such as Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
tests.framing: A doctor may evaluate autoimmune markers if thyroid hormones are abnormal.

questions_for_doctor: Could my cycle irregularities and fatigue be related to an underactive or overactive thyroid?
Would a simple TSH and Free T4 blood test be helpful to confirm or rule this out?
If thyroid hormone levels are borderline, when should we re-test?
things_to_note_before_visit: Track your energy levels and any sensitivity to cold or warm rooms.
Record any noticeable changes in skin dryness, constipation, or heart palpitations.
List any biotin-containing supplements (biotin can interfere with thyroid lab results).

urgency_rules.description: A routine evaluation with a trusted primary care provider is a gentle starting step.

tests.name: Comprehensive General Health Workup
tests.description: Complete blood count (CBC) to screen for anemia, basic metabolic panel, and vital sign review.
tests.framing: A general physician may start with routine health checks and iron levels.

questions_for_doctor: What could be contributing to the symptoms I am feeling?
Would you recommend consulting a specialist like a gynaecologist or endocrinologist?
Are there general health screenings appropriate for my age and symptoms?
things_to_note_before_visit: Write down your chief symptoms and when they started.
Bring a list of all current supplements or medications.
